VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: Verified all relevant boundaries—empty series (trivially convergent, zero partial sums, M=0 works), zero (x=0 gives A(0)=a_0, limit unaffected), one (limit x↑1 is the explicit claim; step 4.1 handles the approach), degenerate (all a_n=0 yields s=0, identity holds), endpoints (x=1 not evaluated, only one‑sided limit), and nonempty‑choice (N chosen from convergence of S_n, x from [0,1)). No counterexample; the classical proof is robust.

SOURCES: Inspected all five supplied items. `def-abel-and-cesaro-summability` matches the theorem’s conclusion exactly. `lem-abel-summation-by-parts` specialises correctly to the finite identity used (with S_n = A_{n+1}). `thm-geometric-series` provides convergence of ∑x^n and its sum; the constant‑multiple step ∑Mx^n is an immediate consequence of sequence limit laws. `lem-convergent-implies-bounded` supplies the uniform bound M. `thm-direct-comparison-test` is applied to non‑negative terms |S_n x^n| ≤ Mx^n and yields absolute convergence. Every citation is accurate and sufficient.

CHECKED: Title, public statement, all four proof steps (1.1–4.4), and Remarks. The only un‑cited inferences are standard within‑30‑second closures (e.g., constant multiple of a convergent series, absolute convergence implies ordinary convergence). The proof is logically valid and complete.
